# Purpose and scope

This document specifies the rotor-noise model v4 and the two procedures that
fit it. The model generates multi-rotor drone noise for the training of speech
enhancement and rotor-speed models.

There is **one model**: one set of parameters, one formula, one renderer, one
payload schema. There are **two fit procedures**:

- **Procedure A, the bench.** It fits the DREGON drone from its single-rotor
  recordings (four motors, five throttle settings each).
- **Procedure B, free flight.** It fits Michael's drone (MD2) from its
  free-flight recordings with telemetry labels.

The two procedures share the model, the priors, the initialisation rule and the
optimiser. They differ only where the data differ: the resolution of the
periodogram, the number of rotors in one recording, and what is measured
independently.

The model must reproduce these properties of real recordings:

1. The harmonic comb of each rotor: the line levels, the line shapes and their
   change with the rotor speed.
2. The broadband floor: its shape, its level and its change with the rotor
   speed.
3. The frame-to-frame flicker of the lines.
4. The differences between the microphones of one array.
5. The wind on some capsules.

The model does not reproduce the room, the propagation path, or the phase
relations between microphones. The downstream consumers read magnitude
spectrograms.

Part 1 gives the model (@sec-model) and its priors (@sec-priors). Part 2 gives
the shared initialisation and optimiser (@sec-shared-fit) and the two
procedures (@sec-bench-fit, @sec-flight-fit). Part 3 gives the evidence
(@sec-evidence) and the known limits (@sec-limits).

# The baseline and the changes {#sec-changes}

The baseline is nv3r4: the noise-model-v3 flight model under the round-4 priors
(`model.PRIORS_V4`; definition `docs/explainers/noise-model-v3-wander.qmd`;
campaign log `docs/experiments/noise-model-v3.md` § Round 4). nv3r4 fitted
Michael's cruise and standby pools and the DREGON free-flight pool without
wander latents. Its renders passed the parity and LTAS criteria of round 4.

v4 keeps from nv3r4:

- one cosine per (rotor, order) on a carrier shared by the orders of the rotor;
- the shaft speed error as an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) process
  [@uhlenbeck1930brownian];
- the floor shape as a 14-point spline with a measured prior scale $\sigma_B$;
- the Whittle likelihood on periodogram cells [@whittle1953];
- the flight front end, the flight shaft treatment, the 64-frame stratified
  L-BFGS subset, the all-frames polish and the four restarts;
- no wander latents;
- the level prior relative to the measured floor (round-4 change C4);
- the identifiability gate and the round-4 acceptance criteria.

| # | Block | nv3r4 | v4 | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Line families | one family; odd orders penalised in the level prior | **aerodynamic** (every $k$) and **motor** ($k = 3pn$) | @sec-ev-families |
| 2 | Profiles | one per rotor, independent | **one per rotor per family**, tied by a hierarchical prior | @sec-ev-profiles |
| 3 | Line speed law | one `amp_exp` per rig | **one exponent per family per rig**, shared by the rotors | @sec-ev-speed-lines |
| 4 | Floor | one floor for the rig, mean speed law $\tfrac1R\sum_r s_r^{b}$ | **one floor per rotor**, shape $F(f)$ and exponent $b(f)$ shared by the rotors; the rig floor is the **sum** | @sec-ev-floor |
| 5 | Line shape | Lorentzian width $\gamma_{rk}$ (random-walk phase) | **two bounded processes per order**: log-amplitude OU and phase OU | @sec-ev-pedestal |
| 6 | Pedestal priors | half-normal $\gamma$ with parity floor | measured amplitude prior with a cap; **half-normal on the phase-pedestal width** with parity | @sec-ev-pedestal |
| 7 | Floor prior | spline with measured $\sigma_B$ | the same, plus a **soft push upward** to the bases of the lines | @sec-ev-floor-push |
| 8 | Shaft on the bench | — | free, with one speed law shared by the rotors | @sec-ev-shaft |
| 9 | Microphones | channels normalised in the data by the array response | in flight the same, **plus a fixed geometric term per rotor–mic pair**; **pair EQ** on the bench; **no per-line scatter** | @sec-ev-mics |
| 10 | Initialisation | warm start from the v2 fit | **from the data and the priors only**; no earlier fit is read | @sec-init |

# The model {#sec-model}

## Notation

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $r = 1 \dots R$ | rotor | – |
| $m = 1 \dots M$ | microphone | – |
| $k = 1 \dots K$ | harmonic order of the shaft rate | – |
| $B$ | number of blades | – |
| $p$ | number of pole pairs of the motor | – |
| $f_r(t)$ | the shaft rate of rotor $r$ (measured on the bench, the label in flight) | rev/s |
| $f_{\rm ref}$ | the reference speed of every level, 80 rev/s | rev/s |
| $s_r(t) = f_r(t)/f_{\rm ref}$ | the relative speed | – |
| $\theta_r(t)$ | the shaft phase error | rad |
| $a_{rk}(t)$ | the log-amplitude process of aerodynamic line $(r,k)$ | neper |
| $\psi_{rk}(t)$ | the phase process of aerodynamic line $(r,k)$ | rad |

All levels are in dB on power. A level $L$ gives the power $10^{L/10}$.

## The signal

$$
x_m(t) = \sum_{r}\sum_{k} h_{mr}(k f_r)\Big[A^{a}_{rk}(t)\cos\!\big(k\phi_r(t)+\psi_{rk}(t)+\varphi^{a}_{rk}\big)
+ \mathbb 1[k=3pn]\,A^{m}_{rk}(t)\cos\!\big(k\phi_r(t)+\varphi^{m}_{rk}\big)\Big] + n_m(t).
$$ {#eq-signal}

- $h_{mr}(f) = 10^{E_{rm}(f)/20}$: the magnitude response from rotor $r$ to
  microphone $m$ (@sec-mic).
- $\varphi^{a}_{rk}$, $\varphi^{m}_{rk}$: fixed random start phases.
- $n_m(t)$: the broadband part (@sec-floor).

Each rotor has two families of lines on the same carrier. The **aerodynamic
family** is present at every order. The **motor family** is present only at
$k = 3pn$, $n = 1, 2, \dots$ At an order that both families occupy, the two
cosines add with independent phases.

## The carrier

$$
\phi_r(t) = 2\pi\!\int_0^t f_r(s)\,ds + \theta_r(t),
\qquad
d\nu_r = -\lambda\nu_r\,dt + \sqrt{2\lambda}\,\sigma_\nu\,dW_r,\quad d\theta_r = \nu_r\,dt .
$$ {#eq-carrier}

The shaft phase error $\theta_r$ is shared by every order and every microphone
of the rotor. Order $k$ carries $k\theta_r$. $\sigma_\nu$ is the stationary
standard deviation of the speed error (rad/s) and $\lambda$ its rate (1/s).
Both follow one speed law, shared by the rotors of the rig:

$$
\sigma_\nu(s) = 2\pi f_{\rm ref}\,\varepsilon\,s^{a_\sigma},\qquad
\lambda(s) = \lambda_{\rm ref}\,s^{b_\lambda}.
$$ {#eq-shaft-law}

The structure function of the increment is
$V_\theta(\tau) = 2\sigma_\nu^2\big[|\tau|/\lambda - (1-e^{-\lambda|\tau|})/\lambda^2\big]$.

## The aerodynamic line

$$
A^{a}_{rk}(t) = \sqrt2\;10^{\big(p^{a}_{rk} + 10\,\alpha^{a}\log_{10}s_r(t)\big)/20}\;
e^{\,a_{rk}(t) - \sigma^2_{A,k}/2}.
$$ {#eq-aero}

- $p^{a}_{rk}$: the mean power of the line at $f_{\rm ref}$ (dB).
- $\alpha^{a}$: the speed exponent of the aerodynamic lines, **one value for
  the rig**.
- $a_{rk}(t)$: a stationary OU in log-amplitude, variance $\sigma^2_{A,k}$,
  rate $\gamma_{A,k}$ (Hz). The term $-\sigma^2_{A,k}/2$ keeps the mean power.
- $\psi_{rk}(t)$: a stationary OU **on the phase itself** (bounded), variance
  $\sigma^2_{\phi,k}$ (rad²), rate $\gamma_{\phi,k}$ (Hz), independent of
  $a_{rk}$.

The pedestal parameters $(\sigma^2_{A,k}, \gamma_{A,k}, \sigma^2_{\phi,k},
\gamma_{\phi,k})$ are per order and shared by the rotors and the
microphones of the rig. They do not depend on the speed.

The lag law of the line is

$$
R_{rk}(\tau) = \exp\!\Big[-\tfrac12 k^2 V_\theta(\tau)\Big]\,
\exp\!\Big[\sigma^2_{A,k}\big(e^{-2\pi\gamma_{A,k}|\tau|}-1\big)\Big]\,
\exp\!\Big[\sigma^2_{\phi,k}\big(e^{-2\pi\gamma_{\phi,k}|\tau|}-1\big)\Big].
$$ {#eq-lag}

The last two factors make a coherent core of power share
$e^{-\sigma^2_{A,k}-\sigma^2_{\phi,k}}$ and a pedestal around it. The
pedestal of one process expands into Lorentzians of half-widths $n\gamma$,
$n \ge 1$, with weights $\sigma^{2n}/n!$. Its power-weighted mean half-width is

$$
W = \gamma\,\frac{\sigma^2}{1-e^{-\sigma^2}} ,
$$ {#eq-width}

which is $\gamma$ for small $\sigma^2$ and $\gamma\sigma^2$ for large
$\sigma^2$. The priors act on $W$ (@sec-priors).

## The motor line

$$
A^{m}_{rk} = \sqrt2\;10^{\big(p^{m}_{rn} + 10\,\alpha^{m}\log_{10}s_r(t)\big)/20},\qquad k = 3pn .
$$ {#eq-motor}

A motor line has no pedestal. Its lag law is the shaft factor alone. Its level
$p^{m}_{rn}$ is free per multiple $n$. Its speed exponent $\alpha^{m}$ is one
value for the rig.

## The microphones {#sec-mic}

$E_{rm}(f)$ is the magnitude response from rotor $r$ to microphone $m$ in dB.
It applies to the lines and to the floor of the rotor.

- **Bench.** $E_{rm}$ is the **pair EQ**: the line levels of microphone $m$
  relative to the microphone mean, smoothed in frequency, measured on the
  rotor's recordings before the fit (`bench_v4.pair_eq`). It is a constant of
  the fit.
- **Flight.** $E_{rm}(f) = A_m(f) + \Delta G_{rm}$, with no fitted parameter:
  - $A_m(f)$ is the measured **array response** of nv3r4 (round-4 amendment
    F13): one curve per microphone, shared by the rotors. The data are divided
    by it before the fit, and the renderer applies it back.
  - $\Delta G_{rm} = G_{rm} - \tfrac1R\sum_{r'} G_{r'm}$ with
    $G_{rm} = -20\log_{10} d_{rm}$, $d_{rm}$ the distance from rotor $r$ to
    microphone $m$ in the rig geometry (MD2: `michaels.get_geometry`). It is
    independent of the frequency. The mean over rotors is removed because
    $A_m$ is measured on the mix of all rotors and already contains it.
    $\Delta G_{rm}$ enters the expected periodogram of the fit and the
    renderer.

There is **no per-line, per-microphone scatter term** $\delta$ in the model
(decision, Dmitrii, 2026-10-21). The variation it carried on the bench stays
in the residual (@sec-ev-mics).

## The floor {#sec-floor}

$$
S_m(f,t) = \sum_r 10^{E_{rm}(f)/10}\,F(f)\,s_r(t)^{\,b(f)} \;+\; F(f)\,s\;+\;N_m(f) \;+\; W_m(f,t),
$$ {#eq-floor}

$$
b(f) = b_0 + b_1\log_2\!\big(f/2\,\mathrm{kHz}\big).
$$ {#eq-floor-exp}

- $F(f) = 10^{(\mu + \sigma_B(Lz)(f))/10}$: the floor of **one rotor** at
  $f_{\rm ref}$, shared by the rotors of the rig. $L$ is the Cholesky factor of
  a squared-exponential kernel over 14 control points on a geometric grid; the
  spline alone carries the level and the tilt (nv3r4).
- $b(f)$: the speed exponent of the floor, shared by the rotors.
- The rig floor is the **sum** over the rotors. In a single-rotor recording
  the sum has one term.
- $s$: a static share for sound that does not scale with the rotor speed.
  Flight only; it is 0 on the bench, where the ambient is measured.
- $N_m(f)$: the measured ambient of the room. Bench only.
- $W_m(f,t)$: the wind on a capsule. On the bench it is one level per
  recording on the windy microphones (the downwash grows with throttle). In
  DREGON flight it is the static per-mic term of nv3r4. MD2 has none.

## The renderer

The renderer draws, per clip and per aerodynamic line, both processes
$a_{rk}(t)$ and $\psi_{rk}(t)$ on the 1 kHz envelope grid of the nv3r4
renderer. The complex envelope of the line is
$10^{(\cdot)/20}\,e^{a_{rk}-\sigma^2_{A,k}/2}\,e^{i\psi_{rk}}$. This
replaces the 2026-10-02 rule that rendered the whole pedestal as amplitude:
that renderer missed the expected spectrum of the R3 bench fit by 1.8–2.6 dB
and over-flickered the lines at $k$ = 40–80 by 2.5–3.5 dB
(`docs/explainers/noise-v4-bench-fit.qmd` § 2–3). The floor is the nv3r4 WOLA
synthesis with the per-rotor gain $\sum_r s_r(t)^{b(f)}$ per bin.

# The priors {#sec-priors}

| Site | Per | Prior | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\bar p^{a}_k$ | rig, order | $\mathcal N(\hat F_k - 12 - 15\,\mathbb 1[k \bmod B \ne 0],\ 10)$ dB | nv3r4 C4; $\hat F_k$ = the measured floor at the line's peak bin in the line's units |
| $p^{a}_{rk} - \bar p^{a}_k$ | rotor, order | $\mathcal N(c^{a}_r, 3.5)$ dB | @sec-ev-profiles |
| $c^{a}_r$, $c^{m}_r$ | rotor | $\mathcal N(0, 2.5)$ dB, mean over rotors pinned at 0 | @sec-ev-profiles |
| $\bar p^{m}_n$ | rig, multiple | $\mathcal N(\hat F_{3pn} - 12,\ 10)$ dB | C4 without the parity penalty |
| $p^{m}_{rn} - \bar p^{m}_n$ | rotor, multiple | $\mathcal N(c^{m}_r, 3.5)$ dB | @sec-ev-profiles |
| $\alpha^{a}$ | rig | $\mathcal N(5.5, 1.0)$ | @sec-ev-speed-lines |
| $\alpha^{m}$ | rig | $\mathcal N(0, 2)$ | @sec-ev-speed-lines |
| $b_0$, $b_1$ | rig | $\mathcal N(3, 1)$; $\mathcal N(0.5, 0.25)$ per octave | @sec-ev-floor |
| $z$ | rig | $\mathcal N(0, I)$, scale $\sigma_B$ measured | nv3r4 |
| floor push | rig | $+\kappa\sum_j \bar c_j$ on the log-prior, $\bar c_j$ the control values in dB | @sec-ev-floor-push |
| $\sigma^2_{A,k}$ | rig, order | LogN$(\log m_{g}, 0.5)$ truncated at $c_{g}$; $(m_g, c_g)$ per order group $g$ in @tbl-amp | @sec-ev-pedestal |
| $\gamma_{A,k}$ | rig, order | LogN$(\log 0.4\,\mathrm{Hz}, 0.5)$ for $k \le 8$; LogN$(\log 1.0\,\mathrm{Hz}, 0.5)$ above | direct amplitude measurement |
| $\sigma^2_{\phi,k}$ | rig, order | LogN$(\log 1, 1.5)$ | wide; the data set it on the bench |
| $W_{\phi,k}$ (@eq-width) | rig, order | HalfNormal$(c_W^{\rm even})$ for $k \bmod B = 0$, HalfNormal$(c_W^{\rm odd})$ otherwise, in Hz | @sec-ev-pedestal; $c_W$ measured in step A0 |
| $\varepsilon$ | rig | HalfNormal$(0.005)$ | bench round R2 |
| $a_\sigma$, $b_\lambda$ | rig | $\mathcal N(1, 0.5)$ | bench round R2 |
| $\lambda_{\rm ref}$ | rig | LogN$(\log 12, 0.5)$ 1/s | bench quick fits |
| wind level | recording or rig, windy mic | $\mathcal N(\text{measured}, 6)$ dB | nv3r4 |
| $s$ | rig (flight) | LogN$(\log 2.5\cdot10^{-3}, 1)$ | nv3r4 |

: The priors of v4. The bench and the flight fit read the same table, except
the shaft (@sec-flight-fit). {#tbl-priors}

| Order group $g$ | $k$ | $m_g$ (median) | $c_g$ (cap) |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| 1 | 1–3 | 0.001 | 0.075 |
| 2 | 4–8 | 0.11 | 0.29 |
| 3 | 9–20 | 0.14 | 0.24 |
| 4 | 21–40 | 0.10 | 0.20 |
| 5 | ≥ 41 | 0.02 | 0.12 |

: The amplitude prior of the pedestal. $m_g$ is the median over the 20 DREGON
bench recordings of the per-recording median log-amplitude variance; $c_g$ is
the largest per-recording 90th percentile (`results/static_rig/single_rotor/amplitude_jitter.json`,
0.25 s frames, calm microphones, lines more than 6 dB over the floor). Group 5
is measured on $k$ = 41–80 and extended to every higher order. {#tbl-amp}

Three properties of the priors matter for the fit:

1. **Unresolved orders sink.** The level prior centres a line 12 dB under the
   floor (27 dB for a non-blade-pass order). A line that the data do not
   resolve stays under the floor instead of building a pedestal. No order is
   switched on or off before the fit (decision, 2026-09-22).
2. **Pedestals stay narrow unless the data ask.** The half-normal on $W_\phi$
   is light-tailed in linear Hz. A broad skirt on a weak line costs more than
   it buys.
3. **The floor is pushed up.** Between the lines, the floor and the pedestal
   skirts explain the same cells. The push breaks that tie toward the floor.
   The Whittle term stops the floor at the bases of the lines.

# Fitting: what both procedures share {#sec-shared-fit}

## The objective

The objective is the Whittle negative log-likelihood summed over the cells of
every recording, every microphone and every frame, minus the log-prior of
@tbl-priors. The parameters are MAP estimates in an unconstrained
parametrisation. There are no latent tracks.

## Initialisation {#sec-init}

Both procedures start the same way. No parameter is read from an earlier fit
of any model generation.

1. **Floor.** For each periodogram (bench: per recording and microphone;
   flight: per frame and microphone), take the minimum of the spectrum in each
   gap between two neighbouring lines of all rotors. Average these minima over
   the periodograms. Take the median within each spline cell to get the 14
   control values. On the bench subtract the ambient. Divide by
   $\sum_r 10^{E_{rm}/10} s_r^{b_{\rm init}}$, with $b$ at its prior centre.
   Solve for $(\mu, z)$ by ridge least squares.
2. **Aerodynamic levels.** For each rotor and order, average the spectral
   height at $k f_r$ over the rotor's recordings or frames. Move each height to
   $f_{\rm ref}$ with $\alpha^{a}$ at its prior centre. Subtract the floor
   initialised in step 1. Convert the height to line power with the line's
   kernel at the initial pedestal. Where the height is under the floor, start
   at the prior centre.
3. **Motor levels.** At $k = 3pn$, set the aerodynamic level to the mean of
   the aerodynamic levels at $k \pm B$. Give the motor line the rest of the
   measured power, or the prior centre where the rest is negative.
4. **Pedestal and shaft.** Restart $j = 0$ takes the prior medians. Restarts
   $j = 1, 2, 3$ draw every pedestal and shaft parameter from its prior.
5. **Exponents.** At the prior centres.
6. **Wind.** At the measured centres.

## The optimiser {#sec-optimiser}

1. Adam, learning rate 0.02, 1500 steps.
2. Strong-Wolfe L-BFGS. Bench: on every cell. Flight: on a 64-frame subset
   stratified over the windows, then one all-frames polish.
3. **Evidence freeze.** After step 2, compute for each order the Fisher
   information of its phase-pedestal parameters from the Whittle term. Where the
   data shrink the prior variance by less than 10 %, hold those parameters at
   the prior median for the rest of the run. Release them for one final
   L-BFGS pass and report its gain. The freeze changes the search, not the
   objective.
4. A fresh-memory L-BFGS restart pass.
5. **Convergence.** A restart is converged when the restart pass gains less
   than $10^{-4}$ nats per cell **and** moves no parameter group by more than
   its tolerance: levels 0.1 dB (median over lines), exponents 0.02, floor
   control values 0.1 dB, log-dynamics 0.05.
6. Four restarts. Keep the lowest objective. Report the spread of every group
   over the restarts.

# Procedure A — the DREGON bench {#sec-bench-fit}

## Data

`DREGON-frames` `motor_Motor{1-4}_{50,60,70,80,90}`: four motors, five
throttle settings each (48–89 rev/s, span 1.8×), 8 microphones, decimated
44.1 → 16 kHz. One periodic-Hann periodogram per microphone over the strict
rotor-on span (9.8–36 s; 0.03–0.1 Hz bins). Band 30 Hz–7.2 kHz.

## Steps

**A0. Measure the pedestal width scale.** Run the per-order phase coherence
(`scripts/static_rig_scratch/one_rotor_coherence.py`) on all 20 recordings,
calm microphones, at lags 2.5, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000
and 2000 ms. Fit $2\sigma^2_\phi(1 - e^{-2\pi\gamma_\phi\tau})$ to the net
phase increment variance of every gated order. Compute $W_\phi$ with
@eq-width. Set $c_W^{\rm even}$ and $c_W^{\rm odd}$ so that the 97.5th
percentile of the measured $W_\phi$ of each parity sits at the half-normal's
97.5th percentile ($2.24\,c_W$). The current lag grid (5 ms, then 10, 20, 50 ms)
does not resolve the fast part: the net variance jumps by 0.2–0.75 rad²
between 20 and 50 ms at $k \ge 8$.

**A1. Span and carrier.** Strict span per recording
(`single_rotor.strict_span`). Refine the carrier on the cores of orders 2–7.
Freeze it (±0.003 rev/s).

**A2. Ambient.** Read the ambient on every rotor-stopped run of the recording
within 2 dB of its 5th-percentile level, at least 1 s from the span
(`bench_v4.ambient_runs`). Store it as $N_m(f)$.

**A3. Pair EQ.** Compute $E_{rm}(f)$ per motor (`bench_v4.pair_eq`). Store it
as a constant.

**A4. Windy microphones.** Motor1 {5, 6}, Motor2 {0}, Motor3 {1, 2}, Motor4
{4} (20–200 Hz power over 1–4 kHz more than 6 dB above the array median). They
get the wind term.

**A5. One joint fit over the 20 recordings.** Shared by the four motors:
$F$, $b_0$, $b_1$, $\alpha^{a}$, $\alpha^{m}$, the pedestal parameters and
the shaft law. Per motor: the profiles $p^{a}_{rk}$, $p^{m}_{rn}$. Per
recording: the frozen carrier, the ambient and the wind levels. Initialise by
@sec-init. Optimise by @sec-optimiser.

**A6. Export** one `noise-v4-fit/3` payload for the DREGON rig: four rotor
profiles per family, the shared laws, the pedestal parameters, the shaft law,
$F$, and per recording the carrier, ambient and wind.

## Checks before acceptance

- **Planted ladder.** Render 20 recordings from known parameters with the v4
  renderer plus the recorded ambients. Fit them with A5. The fit must recover
  the profiles within 1 dB on lines ≥ 10 dB over the floor, $\alpha^{a}$
  within 0.3, $b_0$ within 0.3, the floor within 1 dB, $\varepsilon$ and
  $\lambda_{\rm ref}$ within 20 %, $W_\phi$ within 30 % on lines ≥ 15 dB over
  the floor. **The floor push $\kappa$ is set here:** the smallest value that
  recovers the planted floor within 1 dB.
- **Floor at the bases.** At the midpoints between lines, the fitted expected
  spectrum minus the data is within ±1 dB in every octave band.
- **The four-rotor recording.** Without refitting, predict `motor_allMotors_70`
  (four rotors at 65.7 rev/s mean, carriers 0.83–3.0 Hz apart) from the bench
  payload: four line sets plus the **sum** of the four rotor floors plus its
  ambient. The prediction must match the data within 1.5 dB per octave band
  between the lines, and within 2 dB rms on the line levels of the orders the
  four rotors do not share. This tests the summed-floor rule (@eq-floor).
- **Flicker.** The frame-to-frame level sd at $k$ = 40–80 (64 ms frames) of
  renders must match the recordings (5.5–5.8 dB) within 0.5 dB. This is the
  only check of the amplitude/phase split.
- **Spectrum and sound.** The LTAS, the zoom panels, the fold by line distance
  and the listening clips of `docs/explainers/noise-v4-bench-fit.qmd`, on the
  new fit.
- **Convergence** (@sec-optimiser) on the selected restart.

# Procedure B — free flight on MD2 {#sec-flight-fit}

## Data

Michael's drone (DJI Matrice 100, 4 rotors, 8 microphones). FLY125: the
standby run (1.8–15.3 s; rotors at about 31, 35, 40 and 36 rev/s) and the
cruise windows (68–98 rev/s) of nv3r4, labels as nv3r4 (`rps_refined`).
FLY124 stays the held-out evaluation cohort.

## Front end

The nv3r4 front end: 16 kHz, 2048-point periodic Hann (7.8 Hz bins), hop 512,
frames thinned by 4, composite exposure weights. The pedestal is inside one
bin.

## What the flight fit can and cannot identify

- **Levels, the floor and the speed laws** are identified. The pool spans
  31–98 rev/s (3.2×), wider than the bench ladder.
- **The motor family.** On the standby run only order 84 stands out, on all
  four rotors (@fig-md2-orders). The multiples $n \ne 4$ sink by the level
  prior.
- **The phase pedestal** is not identified at 7.8 Hz. With the half-normal
  prior its MAP would be zero. The flight fit therefore does not fit
  $\sigma^2_{\phi,k}$ or $\gamma_{\phi,k}$; it holds them at the prior
  medians.
- **The amplitude pedestal** shows as frame-to-frame line flicker. The
  Whittle likelihood does not model the correlation of a line's level across
  frames, so it does not identify it. The flight fit sets $\sigma^2_{A,k}$ and
  $\gamma_{A,k}$ from the pool's own block-wander measurement
  (`scripts/noise_v3_measure_wander.py`, $\sigma_v$ and $\tau_v$ per order
  group: $\sigma^2_A = (\sigma_v \ln 10/20)^2$, $\gamma_A = 1/(2\pi\tau_v)$),
  truncated at the caps $c_g$ of @tbl-amp.
- **The shaft** carries the label error as well as the jitter, as in nv3r4.
  The speed law is pinned flat ($a_\sigma = b_\lambda = 0$),
  $\lambda = 2\pi\cdot16$ 1/s (the band edge of the 31 Hz label) and
  $\sigma_\nu \sim$ LogN$(1.68, 0.66)$ rad/s from the telemetry residuals of
  six drones (round-4 changes A1, A2). There is no separate label-error term
  (decision, 2026-10-21): a second OU of the same form as the shaft error
  cannot be told apart from it, and nv3r4, whose shaft term absorbed the label
  error, gave renders that looked and sounded right.

## Steps

**B1. Measure the pool**, latent-free, as nv3r4: $\sigma_B$, $\hat F_k$, the
array response $A_m(f)$, the block wander. Compute $\Delta G_{rm}$ from the
rig geometry (@sec-mic). Store both as constants of the fit.

**B2. One joint fit over the standby and cruise windows.** Shared by the four
rotors: $F$, $b_0$, $b_1$, $s$, $\alpha^{a}$, $\alpha^{m}$, the pedestal
parameters (held as above) and the shaft (pinned as above). Per rotor: the
profiles. Initialise by @sec-init. Optimise by @sec-optimiser. If the
standby–cruise residual check fails, fall back to the nv3r4 arrangement: one
fit per regime, composed in the renderer by the smoothstep in the slowest
rotor's speed (0 at 45 rev/s, 1 at 65 rev/s).

**B3. Gate.** Run the identifiability gate on the fit with the trajectory
frames.

**B4. Export** one `noise-v4-fit/3` payload for the MD2 rig.

## Checks before acceptance

- The round-4 criteria: Michael's parity ratio ≤ 1.05; Michael's LTAS proxy
  ≤ 1.332 dB; the Listen comparison on FLY124.
- **Standby–cruise residual.** The mean residual on the line levels per
  regime is within ±2 dB. A larger gap means one speed law does not hold over
  3.2× for this rig.
- **The motor line.** On standby renders, order 84 stands 7–14 dB over its
  neighbouring half-orders on every rotor, as in the recording.
- **Convergence** (@sec-optimiser).

# From the fits to the generator

A bank entry is a rig payload plus a trajectory. The renderer is the same for
both rigs. The bank laws of the generic drone prior
(`src/experiments/noise_model/drone_prior.py`) are revised from the two fits
once both pass their checks. Until then the round-4 bank policy stays in force.
The revision must read: four profiles per rig with the hierarchical spread of
@tbl-priors, one speed law per family per rig, the summed floor, and the
two-process pedestal.

# Evidence and justification {#sec-evidence}

## Two line families {#sec-ev-families}

**DREGON bench.** The orders 84, 105 and 126 of every motor are 10–21 dB above
their local floor at every throttle. Their power falls or stays constant from
50 % to 90 % throttle: exponents −1.1/−1.3/+1.9/−2.1 at $k = 84$ for motors
1–4 (`results/static_rig/single_rotor/speed_laws.json`). The blade-pass line
of the same recordings follows its law with 0.6 dB rms. The motor orders are
coherent: $|\gamma|$ = 0.7–0.8 at lags 0.5–2 s at $k = 42$, against ≤ 0.3 for
the aerodynamic orders around it (`docs/explainers/order-decoherence.qmd`).

**MD2 standby.** Order 84 is the only motor line. @fig-md2-orders shows the
standby spectrum (3–15 s) resampled on each rotor's own order axis
($k = f/f_r(t)$, telemetry speed every 125 ms). Line height over the
neighbouring half-orders:

| order | rotor 1 | rotor 2 | rotor 3 | rotor 4 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 (blade pass) | 16.3 dB | 13.0 | 6.9 | 10.4 |
| **84** | **7.6** | **13.5** | **7.0** | **13.5** |
| 21, 42, 63, 105, 126 | ≤ 3 | ≤ 3 | ≤ 3 | ≤ 3.8 |

In the raw spectrum the four order-84 lines sit at 2596, 2924, 3050 and
3378 Hz. Each is as wide as its rotor's speed drift over the span. Nothing else
in 2.45–3.5 kHz rises above the floor. 84 is $3pn$ with $p = 7$, $n = 4$. It is
also $12 \times 14$, the cogging order of a 12-slot, 14-pole motor
[INFERENCE: the MD2 motor type is not confirmed].

**Physics.** A permanent-magnet motor radiates at the slot-passing and
commutation multiples of the shaft rate. The cogging force is set by the
magnet–slot geometry, not by the current; its tone can be flat or fall with
speed [INFERENCE]. The loading noise of the blades grows with a high power of
the tip speed [@gojon2021lowre; @zhong2020revisit]. The two sources differ in
origin, speed law and coherence. The model gives them separate families. A
free level per multiple $n$ lets one rig show 42–126 (DREGON) and another only
84 (MD2).

**Multiples of 7 that are not multiples of 21.** On the DREGON bench they rise
8–11 dB above their neighbours at 3.8–5.2 kHz, and only there. Order 56 at
80 % throttle (4380 Hz) reaches +22 dB. A structural mode of the motor that
only the electromagnetic forces excite gives this pattern [INFERENCE]. v4 does
not model it. These lines stay in the residual.

![MD2 FLY125 standby, 3–15 s: the spectrum resampled on each rotor's own order
axis, 8-microphone mean. Dotted: multiples of 21. The broad humps in each panel
are the other rotors' order-84 lines, smeared on the wrong axis.](../../results/noise_v4/md2_motor_orders/md2_standby_orders.png){#fig-md2-orders}

## Four profiles with a common centre {#sec-ev-profiles}

The rotors of one rig are of one type. Their profiles differ by a level offset
and by a scatter per line. The bench gives 3.7 dB between runs per line;
Michael's v3 fits give 4–5.6 dB per line and 2.3–5.2 dB per rotor
(`docs/experiments/static-rig-profiles.md` § Generic drone prior). The
hierarchical prior uses 3.5 dB per line and 2.5 dB per rotor. The spreads are
fixed, not fitted: a jointly maximised spread collapses to zero.

## One speed exponent per family {#sec-ev-speed-lines}

**Measurement.** On the DREGON ladder the blade-pass line gives
$\alpha = 6.2 \pm 0.2$. The even orders 4–40 give a median of 5.3 (10–90 %:
3.4–6.2) **with no trend in $k$**. A separate exponent per order lowers the
residual from 2.4 to 2.1 dB rms only. The per-motor values are 4.5–5.4 at
$k \le 20$ and 4.8–5.7 at $k$ = 22–40: the motors agree within their scatter,
so one exponent per rig suffices.

**Literature.** @gojon2021lowre measured the BPF tone of isolated low-Reynolds
rotors growing as $U^7$, the overall level as $U^6$. @zhong2020revisit show
that unsteady loading governs the higher harmonics. The prior
$\mathcal N(5.5, 1)$ sits between the bench values and the anechoic
literature.

**What the R3 fit showed.** With a free scatter $\delta$ per (recording, mic,
line), $\alpha^{a}$ drifted from 2.9 to 3.6 (Motor1) and from 3.2 to 3.8
(Motor3) between L-BFGS iteration 400 and the end, while the $\delta$ means
per setting fell by about 1 dB at 80–90 %: the level trend with speed could go
either into $\alpha$ or into $\delta$. nv3r4 showed the same confound
(`amp_exp` 9 → 13 between 150 and 600 iterations). Without $\delta$ the
confound is gone.

![The speed laws on the DREGON bench ladder. Left: the per-order exponent of
the line power (blue even orders, orange odd, red multiples of 21). Middle: the
exponent of the floor under harmonic $k$. Right: the exponent of the floor at
fixed frequency, raw and with the rotor-off ambient removed; the thin lines are
the per-motor fits of $b(f) = b_0 + b_1\log_2(f/2\,\mathrm{kHz})$.](../../results/static_rig/single_rotor/speed_laws.png){#fig-speed-laws}

## The floor: per rotor, shared shape, summed {#sec-ev-floor}

**Frequency-dependent exponent.** The floor between the lines grows with speed
with an exponent of 5.1 at 100–200 Hz, 1.3–1.4 at 0.4–1.6 kHz and 3.2–4.2
above 3.2 kHz (pooled over the motors, se 0.1–0.3). The law
$b_0 + b_1\log_2(f/2\,\mathrm{kHz})$ fits the four motors with
$b_0$ = 2.35–2.60 and $b_1$ = 0.42–0.60 per octave. A Strouhal-scaled floor
leaves 2.0–2.5 dB against 1.2–1.4 dB for the fixed-frequency axis.

**Shared shape.** The four DREGON motors are one type. A floor shape per motor
would add 3 × 15 parameters that the single-rotor recordings cannot tell
apart from the pair EQ. One shape for the rig, entered through each pair's
EQ, keeps the rotor differences in the profiles.

**Summed in flight.** The broadband sources of different rotors are
independent. Their powers add. nv3r4 wrote the rig floor as one floor times
the mean speed factor; v4 writes one floor per rotor and sums them, so that a
bench fit and a flight fit read the same $F$. The DREGON four-rotor recording
tests the rule (@sec-bench-fit).

## The floor push {#sec-ev-floor-push}

Between two lines the data can be explained by the floor or by the pedestal
skirts of the neighbouring lines. In the R3 bench fit the skirts took the
space: on Motor1, $W$ reached a median of 23 Hz at $k$ = 30–80 and 28 Hz at
$k$ = 80–146, and the floor fell to about
−80 dB above 400 Hz, under the data, where nothing identified it. In nv3r4 the
same space was taken by the floor because the lines were needles. The push
gives the tie to the floor; the half-normal on $W_\phi$ limits the skirts;
the Whittle term forbids a floor above the data. $\kappa$ is the smallest value
that recovers a planted floor (@sec-bench-fit).

## The pedestal: amplitude and phase {#sec-ev-pedestal}

**Measurement.** On `motor_Motor1_70` (mic 2), after the removal of the shaft:

- $k$ = 1–3: amplitude and phase are steady (≤ 0.03 rad² and ≤ 0.01 neper² at
  2 s).
- $k = 4$: the fluctuation is amplitude (log-amplitude variance 0.1, net phase
  variance 0.01 rad² at 500 ms).
- $k \ge 8$: the log-amplitude increment variance plateaus at 0.25–0.48
  ($\sigma^2_A \approx$ 0.12–0.24). The phase loses 0.2–0.75 rad² within
  50 ms and then grows to its ceiling (≥ 1.5 rad²) for $k \ge 12$.

So at high orders the pedestal is mostly phase. Over the 20 bench recordings
the amplitude part is small and bounded (@tbl-amp).

**Why both processes, why a cap on amplitude.** No periodogram, long or
short, separates the two: both give the same factor in @eq-lag. The split
matters only for what a magnitude model sees frame to frame: amplitude makes a
line flicker; phase noise does not. The amplitude prior centres the split on
the direct measurement and caps it. The phase takes the rest of the measured
pedestal. A render with the whole pedestal in amplitude over-flickered by
2.5–3.5 dB (@sec-model, the renderer).

**Why a width prior.** Without one, the R3 bench fit gave the odd low orders a
faint broad skirt: $W$ = 22–60 Hz at $\sigma^2 \approx 0.02$ on Motor1
$k$ = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, against 1.5–4.7 Hz on the even orders. The direct
measurement shows $k$ = 1–3 coherent. nv3r4's width prior with a parity floor
(odd 3 Hz, even 1 Hz) prevented this; v4 applies the same idea to $W_\phi$.

**Physics.** Haystacking: unsteady blade loading from ingested turbulence that
successive blades cut many times gives a per-order complex envelope with a
coherent core, bounded, independent across orders, growing with the order
[@hanson1974spectrum; @majumdar1998ingested; @alexander2017haystacking;
@raposo2024ingestion]. The motor tones have no loading pulse behind them and
carry no pedestal.

## The shaft {#sec-ev-shaft}

On the bench the shaft speed error is an OU process: the line widths grow as
$k^{1.4\text{–}1.9}$. The R3 bench fit gives $\lambda$ = 12–30 1/s and
$\sigma_\nu$ = 0.49–0.83 rad/s on Motor1 and $\lambda$ = 19–32 1/s on
Motor3, close to the quick fits (9–15 1/s). The R1 fit, with the pedestal
capped at $\sigma^2 \le 0.6$, drove $\lambda$ to 25–9058 1/s: the shaft
supplied the line wings that the capped pedestal could not. In flight the
label residual dominates (2.7–11.3 rad/s on six rigs) and nv3r4's pinned
treatment stays (@sec-flight-fit). @zhu2026unsteady and @zhong2023unsteady
measured the sidebands that unsteady rotation adds around the BPF harmonics;
in the model that is the shaft term, common to the orders.

## Microphones {#sec-ev-mics}

The DREGON array is in the near field of each rotor above about 1.5 kHz. The
spread of a rotor's line levels across microphones is 3.6–4.0 dB rms. A fixed
per-pair transfer on the frequency axis explains 45 % of it (the pair EQ).

The R3 bench fit carried the rest as $\delta$ per (recording, mic, line):
4.0–4.35 dB rms, symmetric, mildly heavy-tailed. About 45 % of the
per-microphone part repeats across recordings within 15 Hz; the part common to
the microphones repeats only 0.2–0.3. The recordings were made with the drone
hanging on a string, held by an operator, in rooms with $T_{60} < 150$ ms
[Strauss et al., IROS 2018]: the geometry is not fixed from one recording to the
next.

v4 drops $\delta$ (decision, 2026-10-21), as nv3r4 dropped its latents. The
risk: the shared parameters can absorb level mismatch. In R3 the pedestal of
$k = 56$ grew to $\sigma^2 = 1.6$ to spread the power of a line that one
setting lifted by 22 dB. The planted check and the comparison with the R3
shared parameters (@sec-bench-fit) measure this risk.

**MD2: the rotor-specific response is the geometry.** The array response
$A_m(f)$ (`results/noise_v2/mic_gains/mic_gains.json`,
`rigs.michaels.levels_db.full`: each microphone's deviation from the array
mean, 24 third-octave bands 34 Hz–6.8 kHz, mean over 11 FLY125 windows)
spans about 12 dB across the microphones, with a window-to-window sd of
0.65 dB (median). It is mostly a constant gain per microphone, with a tilt at
4–7 kHz on mics 0, 3 and 7. To test for a response per rotor, every line of
FLY125 (171 s, the flight front end, calibrated telemetry) was kept where it
was more than 11.7 Hz from every line of the other rotors and at least 6 dB
over the local floor. Each rotor's level per microphone and octave band, minus
the mean over the rotors, gives the rotor-specific part:

| band | rotor-specific sd | split-half correlation | slope on $\Delta G_{rm}$ | residual after $\Delta G_{rm}$ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 250–500 Hz | 0.68 dB | 0.80 | 1.14 | 0.26 dB |
| 500–1000 Hz | 0.74 dB | 0.93 | 1.16 | 0.36 dB |
| 1–2 kHz | 0.54 dB | 0.94 | 0.85 | 0.26 dB |
| 2–4 kHz | 0.43 dB | 0.63 | 0.57 | 0.29 dB |

The residual after the geometric term is near the noise of the estimate
(0.2 dB). Below 250 Hz rotors 2 and 4 have too few isolated lines (they run
within 1.5 rev/s of each other in cruise); above 4 kHz no rotor has enough.
Above 2 kHz the measured term is smaller than the geometric prediction (slope
0.57), consistent with scattering by the body at short wavelengths
[INFERENCE]. The geometric term is used at every frequency without a slope.
$|\Delta G_{rm}| \le 1.0$ dB on MD2 (sd 0.55 dB), so at 2–4 kHz the term
overstates the rotor-specific part by 0.24 dB rms, 0.43 dB at most.

## The Whittle likelihood on both supports

The periodogram cell of a Gaussian process is exponential with mean equal to
the expected periodogram [@whittle1953]. The bench support resolves the
pedestals and the shaft cores, so the bench fit identifies the dynamics. The
flight support (7.8 Hz bins) does not, so the flight fit identifies the
levels, the floor and the speed laws, and takes the dynamics from priors and
measurements. The two procedures follow from the two resolutions.

# Known limits {#sec-limits}

1. **The amplitude/phase split** rests on the amplitude prior. No likelihood
   term identifies it. The flicker check tests it on the bench only.
2. **The phase pedestal in flight** is the prior median, not a measurement of
   MD2.
3. **One speed law per family over 3.2×** on MD2 is untested. The fallback is
   the nv3r4 regime composition.
4. **Resonance-shaped lines** (DREGON odd orders 9–13 at 0.4–1.6 kHz, the
   multiples of 7 at 3.8–5.2 kHz) are not in the model.
5. **Per-line scatter** is not in the model. The renderer gives every
   microphone the rotor's mean line level times the pair EQ.
6. **The floor rule** (summed per-rotor floors) is tested on one recording
   (`motor_allMotors_70`).
7. **The rotor–microphone term in flight** is the spherical-spreading
   correction from the geometry. It is measured on MD2 at 250 Hz–4 kHz only;
   below and above it is an extrapolation.
